ready2_open_rewrite.final_cot: Image description: The attached figure is a voltage-divider biased common-emitter amplifier circuit. The upper power rail is labeled +Vcc; the collector is connected through Rc to +Vcc; the emitter is connected through Re to ground, and Ce is connected in parallel with Re; on the left side of the base, Rb2 is connected from +Vcc to the base node, and Rb1 is connected from the base node to ground, forming voltage-divider bias; the input terminal is coupled through C1 to the base; the output terminal is coupled from the collector through C2 to the right-side load RL. Reasoning: According to DC analysis, C1, C2, and Ce in the figure are all regarded as open circuits, so the input source, output load RL, and bypass capacitor do not participate in the quiescent operating point calculation. According to the specified method, in the base voltage divider, Rb2 is the upper resistor and Rb1 is the lower resistor, so VB = 12 × 5 / (15 + 5) = 3.0 V. It is known that UBEQ = 0.7 V, so VE = VB - UBEQ = 3.0 - 0.7 = 2.3 V. The emitter current IE ≈ VE / Re = 2.3 V / 2.3 kΩ = 1.0 mA, approximately IC ≈ IE = 1.0 mA. The collector voltage VC = VCC - IC Rc = 12 - (1.0 mA)(5.1 kΩ) = 6.9 V. Therefore UCEQ = VC - VE = 6.9 - 2.3 = 4.6 V.
